clue.text: Change design of screw around

indicators.note: around tells us to turn the word for the prison officer end to end

parts.note: screw is British prison slang for a warder

explanation.surface: Someone redesigns a crew's arrangement, or turns a screw round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns WARDER backwards. A screw is slang for a prison officer.
explanation.definitionFit: To redraw a plan is to alter its layout by drafting it again.

clue.text: Shot almost lands in river — one's been fired

indicators.note: lands in says the shot ends up inside the river name

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon

indicators.note: almost says the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a pellet is a piece of shot

explanation.surface: A shot nearly hits, then lands in the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last letter of the shot word; 'lands in' puts the rest inside a river in Devon. 'fired' means sacked, not shot from a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: An expellee is someone driven out or dismissed.

clue.text: Cut down, tree seen to come up again

parts.note: to reap is to cut down a crop
a pear is a fruit tree

explanation.surface: A felled tree is seen to sprout again.
explanation.definitionFit: To reappear is to show up once more.

clue.text: Robin Hood robbed so enthusiastically

parts.note: the outlaw robbed in company with his man Will Scarlet, and the idiom for heartily is the same phrase

explanation.surface: The outlaw went about his thieving with relish.
explanation.walkthrough: Will Scarlet was one of Robin Hood's merry men, so the idiom for zestfully also says he robbed alongside Will.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something heartily and eagerly is doing it with gusto, the idiom with a capital-free name in it.

clue.text: Female gets correct cow

parts.note: to righten is to set right, i.e. correct

explanation.surface: A woman puts a cow right, a farmyard tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cow' is a verb here, meaning to intimidate, not the farm animal.
explanation.definitionFit: To cow someone is to scare them into submission.

clue.text: I might not be free to take new order at present

indicators.note: to take new order says the letters of the phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: A prisoner fearing a new court order keeps them locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a court order; 'to take new order' rearranges all fifteen letters of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: For now, temporarily, until things change, is what at present means.

clue.text: Troublemaker effects change of leadership in foreign government!

indicators.note: change of leadership says the first letter of the seat of government is swapped for another

parts.note: the Kremlin stands for the Russian government

explanation.surface: An agitator forces a coup in a foreign regime.
explanation.walkthrough: Change the first letter of KREMLIN, the Moscow seat of power, from K to G.
explanation.definitionFit: A gremlin is an imaginary mischievous sprite blamed for faults in machinery.

clue.text: Absurdly altering figure

indicators.note: absurdly says the following word is rearranged in a crazy way

explanation.surface: Changing a number in a ridiculous fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: A triangle is a three-sided geometric shape.

clue.text: Lunatic — he will constitute a hard case

parts.note: nuts means crazy, lunatic
he'll is the contraction of he will

explanation.surface: A madman will become a tough customer.
explanation.definitionFit: A nutshell is the hard outer casing of a nut.

clue.text: Second dish in messy spread

parts.note: a platter is a large serving dish

explanation.surface: A second course arrives amid a chaotic buffet.
explanation.definitionFit: A splatter is a messy splash of liquid spread around.

clue.text: Tribute paid after death of Yorkshire writer

definitions.meaning: a feudal payment to a lord, often the best beast, due on a tenant's death
the Yorkshire vet-author James Herriot, whose pen name is spelt with a double R

explanation.surface: A tribute is paid after a Yorkshire author dies.
explanation.walkthrough: The writer's pen name is spelt HERRIOT, so the second definition is approximate; the feudal due is the exact sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A heriot was a death duty owed to a feudal lord; Herriot wrote vet stories set in the Yorkshire Dales.

clue.text: Careless hit-and-run

parts.note: to slap is to hit
to dash is to run

explanation.surface: A careless hit-and-run accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hit-and-run' reads as one crime but splits into two verbs joined by 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapdash work is hasty and careless.

clue.text: Sew up American girth split by extra pound

indicators.note: split by says the girth word is opened up and something put in the gap

parts.note: cinch is the American word for a saddle girth
L is the abbreviation for a pound (libra), here added as an extra

explanation.surface: Fastening a horse's girth with an extra pound of weight.
explanation.definitionFit: To sew up a deal is to settle it, i.e. clinch it.

clue.text: Flying bomb comes within an iota somehow, of flying

indicators.note: comes within says the bomb sits inside the rearranged letters
somehow says the letters of an iota are jumbled

parts.note: the V1 was the German flying bomb of WWII, written VI

explanation.surface: A flying bomb lands within an iota of its target.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges AN IOTA into AATION; 'comes within' puts VI (the V1 flying bomb) after its first A.
explanation.definitionFit: Aviation is the art of flight in aircraft.

clue.text: New organ isn't under control

indicators.note: new says the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A newly installed organ refuses to be controlled.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone kept like a puppet is dominated and manipulated by another.

clue.text: Sound of exposed brook

indicators.note: Sound of says we want a word that is said like the next one

parts.note: bare means exposed or uncovered

explanation.surface: The noise of a stream running over open ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brook' looks like a stream; it is the verb meaning to tolerate.
explanation.definitionFit: To brook something is to tolerate or put up with it.

clue.text: Support from nanny, might one think?

definitions.text: Support from nanny, might one think?

parts.words: Support from nanny, might one think?
parts.note: a nanny goat butts, so a female butter might whimsically take the feminine ending -ess

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a childminder provides support.
explanation.walkthrough: The nanny is a goat, not a childminder: a goat that butts is a butter, and the feminine ending -ess makes a female one, as the question mark admits.
explanation.definitionFit: A buttress is a projecting structure built against a wall to support it.

clue.text: Versatile new drivers used in a game of golf

parts.note: L plates mark learner drivers, so two learners are LL
a round is a game of golf

explanation.surface: Flexible new clubs used on a golf course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drivers' suggests golf clubs; they are learner motorists, L each.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-round player is versatile, competent in many areas.

clue.text: List some of the elements

indicators.note: some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Enumerating a few chemical elements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'List' is not a catalogue but a ship leaning over.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that heels over leans to one side, as when it lists.

clue.text: Delicate weed seen in large numbers? On the contrary

indicators.note: seen in would put the garden tool inside the numbers, but the contrary tag swaps them
On the contrary reverses the container relation just described

parts.note: to hoe is to weed
thous is short for thousands

explanation.surface: A fragile weed that turns up in great quantities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' flips 'weed seen in large numbers', so the numbers go inside the weeding tool instead. THOUS is a recognised short form of thousands.
explanation.definitionFit: Hothouse as an adjective describes something sheltered and fragile, like a greenhouse plant.

clue.text: Weird desire suppressed by churchman, lacking some energy

indicators.note: in a down clue, suppressed by puts the desire under the churchman
lacking some says a letter is taken out of the churchman

parts.note: an elder is a church official
an itch is a craving or desire

explanation.surface: A strange urge held down by a cleric who has run out of steam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking some energy' drops only one of the two Es from the churchman; in a down clue 'suppressed by' puts the desire underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Eldritch means eerie and unearthly.

clue.text: In the past, following sound lead

indicators.note: following places the past-time word after the word for sound

parts.note: to plumb is to sound, measure depth
ago means in the past

explanation.surface: Historically, someone followed a sound lead.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumbago is an old name for graphite, the black lead of pencils.

clue.text: Crucial note to bigwig held up

indicators.note: held up in a down clue says the whole run reads upwards

parts.note: la is a note of the sol-fa scale
a VIP is a very important person

explanation.surface: An important memo to a VIP is delayed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held up' turns LA + TO + VIP upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Pivotal means central, the point on which things turn.

clue.text: Finishes off what the banks control to grow rich

indicators.note: Finishes off says the last letter of each word of the phrase is removed

parts.note: a river is held in by its banks, so the phrase is the river

explanation.surface: Banks controlling their money to become wealthy.
explanation.walkthrough: Banks are river banks, not money lenders. 'Finishes off' drops the last letter of THE and of RIVER.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrive is to prosper or flourish.

clue.text: Look for murderers

definitions.meaning: ... (hook) is Cockney rhyming slang for a look

explanation.surface: A detective searching for killers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Have a butcher's' is British slang for take a look, from rhyming slang butcher's hook = look.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a glance, and brutal slaughterers of people.

clue.text: Agree it's sufficient to drop ad

indicators.note: to drop says the advert letters are taken away from the word

parts.note: adequate means sufficient
taken as written

explanation.surface: Consenting that it is enough to cancel the advert.
explanation.definitionFit: To equate things is to treat them as matching or corresponding.

clue.text: Home I left before a year — that's an injustice

parts.note: in means at home
quit means left, departed

explanation.surface: Someone resents leaving home before a year was up.
explanation.definitionFit: An iniquity is a grossly unfair act, a wickedness.

clue.text: Lied translated into our equivalent indirectly

indicators.note: into says the jumbled letters go inside the English word

parts.note: the English counterpart of a German Lied is a song

indicators.note: translated says the letters of Lied are rendered anew

explanation.surface: A German art song rendered in English, approximately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translated' rearranges the letters of Lied into IDEL; 'into' puts them inside the English word, which the clue reaches by its German meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidelong look is oblique, cast sideways rather than straight.

clue.text: German writer follows essay with English article

parts.note: an essay is an attempt, a go
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A German author follows his essay with an English piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Goethe was the great German poet and dramatist of Faust.
